subtopic: Reading 91.1 Guidance for Standards I(A) and I(B)
question_en: To comply with the Standard on independence and objectivity, an analyst making investment recommendations:
option_a: may use outside research only after verifying its accuracy.
option_b: must use only his own research.
option_c: must use only his own or his company's research.
explanation_en: Standard I(B), Independence and Objectivity: the analyst is allowed to use outside research only after an insightful review. There are no restrictions regarding the exclusive use of in- house information.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.1 Guidance for Standards I(A) and I(B) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.1 Guidance for Standards I(A) and I(B)
question_en: Susan Nielsen, CFA, is an equity research analyst on a fact-finding property tour with 6 other analysts to learn about Just Kittens, Inc. Just Kittens sells tungsten ball-bearings and has 16 warehouses, and 20 manufacturing, research, and wholesale sales outlets scattered over 8 countries – mostly emerging markets. Because of the remote location of some of the facilities, commercial travel is effectively unavailable. Just Kittens charters a jet and various busses to take the research analysts to the properties. If Nielsen accepts these accommodations, she is most likely:
option_a: in violation of Standard I(B) "Independence and Objectivity."
option_b: not in violation of Standard I(B) "Independence and Objectivity" because best practices dictate that better access to company executives is likely to lead to more accurate and timely information.
option_c: not in violation of Standard I(B) "Independence and Objectivity" because commercial travel is effectively unavailable.
explanation_en: Nielsen is not in violation of Standard I(B) "Independence and Objectivity" because commercial travel is effectively unavailable.

subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: Which of the following is most likely permitted under Standard I(C), Misrepresentation?
option_a: Citing quotes attributed to "investment experts" without specific reference.
option_b: Including data showing the current government bond yield curve in a report to a client without stating its source.
option_c: Using excerpts from reports prepared by others without acknowledgement.
explanation_en: The government bond yield curve is factual information that is available from many recognized financial or statistical reporting services.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: A money manager works for a full-service brokerage firm. After meeting with a new client and gathering all relevant information, the money manager says that she thinks her firm can perform all the financial services the new client needs. With respect to the Standard on misrepresentation, this statement:
option_a: is not a violation if it is based on the factual information gathered.
option_b: is a violation.
option_c: would only be a violation if it is made in writing.
explanation_en: There is no violation if the opinion is based upon the factual information gathered and the firm's actual capabilities. This is true whether or not the representation was written, oral, or electronic.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: An analyst belongs to a nationally recognized charitable organization, which requires dues for membership. The analyst has worked out a deal under which he provides money management advice in lieu of paying dues. While performing services for the organization, the analyst discovers some useful computer programs that his predecessor developed and left as the property of the organization. The analyst decides to use the computer programs in his consulting business. This action is:
option_a: a violation of Standard I(D) concerning misconduct.
option_b: a violation of Standard III(B) concerning fair dealing.
option_c: appropriate since the analyst is technically an employee of the organization.
explanation_en: Since the programs are the property of the organization, the analyst can only use them for the organization. It does not matter whether the analyst is an employee or not. Personal use of the programs without permission from the charitable organization is dishonest and prohibited.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: Jerry Brock, CFA, is a partner in a small investment advisory firm that caters to high net worth individuals. He has experienced a number of financial setbacks in his personal life over the past two years and has filed for bankruptcy protection. Brock does not inform his clients of this. Has Brock violated CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct?
option_a: Yes, because a member must conduct both personal and professional business in a manner that protects their reputation and integrity.
option_b: Yes, because he must disclose the bankruptcy filing to his clients.
option_c: No.
explanation_en: Declaring personal bankruptcy does not, by itself, reflect adversely on a member or candidate's integrity or trustworthiness. Only if the circumstances of the bankruptcy included fraud or dishonesty on the part of the member would it violate Standard I(D) Misconduct. Standard VI(A) Disclosure of Conflicts does not require members and candidates to disclose personal matters unless they create the appearance of a conflict of interest.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: All of the following are violations of Standard I(D), Misconduct, EXCEPT:
option_a: conviction of a misdemeanor involving civil disobedience in support of one’s personal beliefs.
option_b: any conduct that undermines confidence that the CFA charter represents a level of achievement based on merit and ethical conduct.
option_c: conviction of a crime involving fraud.
explanation_en: The Code and Standards do not focus on personal conduct as long as the conduct does not reflect poorly on one's professional reputation, integrity, or competence.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: Which of the following actions most likely violates Standard I(D) Misconduct?
option_a: A Level I candidate submits a request to her employer for auto travel reimbursement using inflated mileage totals.
option_b: A member pursues an employment opportunity with a competing firm, primarily as a means of securing a salary increase from her current employer.
option_c: An analyst is arrested for trespassing while participating in an anti-abortion protest.
explanation_en: Any activity that reflects adversely on a member's professional reputation, integrity, or competence is a violation of Standard I(D) Misconduct. Standard I(D) is generally not intended to extend to legal transgressions resulting from acts of civil disobedience in support of personal beliefs. A member can pursue an employment opportunity with a competitor as long as the member abides by the Standards related to Duties to Employers.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: Sandra Bulow, CFA, is responsible for updating her employing firm's website to include changes in analysis techniques and trading procedures. She is often very delinquent in making these changes, despite working extensive hours. She is aware clients are using the website to make investment decisions, and has received complaints from the sales department as the information on the website if often different from what is presented in sales meetings. Bulow is most likely:
option_a: in violation of Standard I(C) "Misrepresentation."
option_b: in violation of Standard III(B) "Fair Dealing."
option_c: not in violation of any Standard.
explanation_en: Bulow is most likely in violation of Standard I(C) "Misrepresentation." The web site information is erroneous, and needs to be updated to match the firm's current practices.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: Marc Randall, CFA, is an investment analyst. During a meeting with a potential client, Randall's boss states that, "You can be sure our investments will always outperform Treasury Bonds because of our fine research staff members, like Marc." Randall knows that this statement is:
option_a: a violation of duciary duties owed to clients under the Standards.
option_b: a violation of the Standard concerning prohibition against misrepresentation.
option_c: not in violation of the Code and Standards.
explanation_en: Under Standard I(C), members are forbidden from guaranteeing a specific rate of return on volatile investments. Therefore, the statement is in violation of the Standard.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: A CFA charterholder in a managerial position is in the process of hiring new analysts. If the charterholder conducts background checks on the job applicants with respect to their character, the charterholder has:
option_a: complied with Standard I(D) concerning professional misconduct.
option_b: complied with Standard VII(A) concerning conduct of members and candidates in the CFA Program.
option_c: violated the Code of Ethics by invading the applicants' privacy.
explanation_en: To avoid potential problems and comply with Standard I(D), employers are encouraged to conduct background checks on potential employees.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: Which of the following least likely violates the Standard concerning misconduct? Roland Lawson, a financial analyst:
option_a: drinks excessively during business meetings with clients and returns to work under the influence of alcohol.
option_b: is arrested for participating in a nonviolent protest.
option_c: committed perjury in connection with a lawsuit against his firm.
explanation_en: Guidance for Standard I(D) Misconduct recognizes civil disobedience as an activity that is not a violation. The focus of the Standard is on professional conduct, not personal conduct, unless the personal conduct involves dishonesty, fraud, or deceit.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: Based on CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct, which of the following statements is a violation of Standard I(C), Misrepresentation?
option_a: A broker says XYZ stock is very likely to double in value over the next six months.
option_b: A young trainee bond trader tells a prospective client that she can assist the client in all the client's investment needs: equity, fixed income, and derivatives and based on her years of experience as an analyst in the business that an investment looks like it has lots of potential.
option_c: An investment manager recommends to a prospective client an investment in GNMA bonds because they are guaranteed by the federal government.
explanation_en: CFA Institute members, CFA charterholders, and CFA candidates are prohibited from misrepresenting their services or qualifications and inappropriate assurances about any investment or its return.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: A CFA charterholder takes a trip for which his firm will pay the expenses. Upon his return, he alters some of the numbers on restaurant receipts to inflate the expenses by about one half of a percent. Is this a violation of the Code and Standards?
option_a: This is a violation only if the amount in question is material.
option_b: Yes, because the charterholder should have paid his own expenses.
option_c: Yes, because it reects dishonesty.
explanation_en: Any action by a member or candidate involving dishonesty, fraud, or deceit is a violation of Standard I(D) Misconduct.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: An analyst preparing a report needs to cite which of the following?
option_a: A recent quote from the Federal Reserve Chairman.
option_b: Estimates of betas provided by Standard & Poor's.
option_c: The individual who developed a chart from the same rm.
explanation_en: Statistics provided by a recognized agency, such as Standard and Poor's, do not need to be cited. Charts, quotes, and algorithms developed by the firm would need to be cited when they are used but the individual(s) who developed the materials within the firm do not need to be cited.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: Which of the following are recommended procedures of compliance according to Standard I(D), Misconduct?
option_a: Conduct background checks on potential employees to ensure that they are of good character.
option_b: Enroll employees in a continuing education program that would provide updates on required ethical behavior.
option_c: Refer to the Professional Conduct Program for arbitration of disputes with other members or candidates.
explanation_en: According to Standard I(D) Misconduct - Procedures for Compliance: Members should encourage their employers to conduct background checks on potential employees to ensure that they are of good character and eligible to work in the investment industry.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: The following information involves two research analysts at a brokerage firm. Erik Bagenot, CFA, is preparing a research report on Global Enterprises, Inc. In preparing the report, he uses materials from many sources. For example, he uses factual information published by Standard & Poor's Corporation without acknowledging the source. He also uses excerpts from a research report prepared by another analyst. Bagenot makes only a slight change in wording for these excerpts, but acknowledges the source. Sally Wain, who is currently enrolled in the CFA program, is preparing a research report on Manson Telecommunications. She attends a conference in which several investment experts provide their views about the future prospects of this company. Wain cites several quotations from these investment experts in her report without specific reference. According to CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct involving prohibition against plagiarism, which of the following statements is CORRECT?
option_a: Wain violated the Standards, but Bagenot did not.
option_b: Both Bagenot and Wain violated the Standards.
option_c: Bagenot violated the Standards, but Wain did not.
explanation_en: Bagenot complied with Standard I(C), which permits publishing factual information from Standard & Poor's without acknowledgment and using excerpts with acknowledgment. Wain committed plagiarism because she failed to give specific references for the quotations that she used.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: Which of the following would be permissible under Standard I(C), Misrepresentation?
option_a: Including a graph showing the central bank’s discount rates over the previous 12 months in a report that goes to clients, without citing the source from which the data were gathered.
option_b: Reporting statistics prepared by an outside firm, identifying the source but omitting caveats and qualifying statements.
option_c: Using excerpts from a report prepared by a well known outside research firm without acknowledgement.
explanation_en: The only permissible action in the above list is including a graph of the Fed's discount rates over the last 12 months because it is factual information published by a recognizable financial and statistical reporting service.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: According to CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct, which of the following statements about the prohibition against plagiarism is most accurate? The prohibition against plagiarism applies to written materials:
option_a: oral communications, and telecommunications.
option_b: only.
option_c: and oral communications only.
explanation_en: The prohibition against plagiarism applies to all three areas.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Ethical and professional standard\Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D) - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 91.2 Guidance for Standards I(C) and I(D)
question_en: Hillary Jones, CFA, sometimes promises clients that she will allocate more shares from oversubscribed initial public offerings (IPOs) than she knows she will actually be able to deliver. Her employer has reprimanded her in the past for similar behavior. Which of the following statements is least accurate regarding Jones' behavior?
option_a: Her actions are a violation of the standard concerning professional misconduct because she deceived her clients.
option_b: Her actions are a violation of the standard concerning misrepresentation, because she promised something she knew the firm could not deliver.
option_c: Her actions are a violation of the Standards only if prosecution results in a felony conviction.
explanation_en: Jones violated Standard I(C) Misrepresentation by promising clients she would allocate more shares than she could deliver. Her actions also violated Standard I(D) Misconduct pertaining to acts of dishonesty, fraud, or deceit which reflects adversely on a member's professional reputation, integrity, or competence. She also violated the Code of Ethics which states that members and candidates must act with integrity, competence, diligence, respect, and in an ethical manner with the public, clients, and prospective clients. The specific punishment for the actions is not relevant.
